name: DialSim
ontology_notes: Eval of a TV-show character answering spontaneous quizzes from long multi-party scripts, not a memory engine. LongDialQA uses Friends, The Big Bang Theory, and The Office. Table 2. Friends 335,439 tokens and 788 sessions. TBBT 367,636 tokens and 805 sessions. The Office 352,914 tokens and 2,347 sessions. About 1,000+ question candidates per session. Agent plays the main character (Ross, Sheldon, or Michael). Names are anonymized or swapped so pretrained canon cannot carry the score. User modeled is a scripted TV character in a multi-party scene. Metric scores multiple-choice accuracy, including unanswerable items that must pick (E) I don't know. Misses holes 1 identity drift after 50+ companion sessions, 2 socially wrong timing of a known fact, 3 joke-as-fact, 4 retcon vs lie vs narrator, 5 two companions on one backend, 6 lore vs lived event, 7 poisoning, 9 forget-that, 10 three-month reunion. Hole 8 is adjacent via the time budget.

supersession.evidence: TKG questions use dated quadruples so a past boyfriend can be a distractor for a later date. That is time-indexed relation state, not a scored overwrite of a stored fact. Kim et al. arXiv 2406.13144v6 §3.1.3-§3.1.4.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Sessions carry broadcast-derived dates. Fan quizzes get dated variants. TKG one-hop and two-hop questions ask who was X on a date, including future facts that must be unknown. Table 2 and §3.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: The agent is one named TV character among several speakers. Name-swap adversarial tests pretrained identity versus dialogue. Not user versus companion versus lore as store types.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Unanswerable questions are 20% of the multiple-choice mix. Gold is (E) I don't know when the character was not in the scene or the fact is in the future. That is missing-evidence abstention, not trauma, kink, or spoiler silence.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Name swapping conflicts with pretrained canon. No stored-text jailbreak of a system persona.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that items. History is the script plus optional RAG store.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Project site frames 1s / 3s / 5s time limits. simulator.py --sleep_time default 5 seconds. Timeout on save, retrieve, or answer is scored Wrong. Paper v6 Table 3 reports Friends accuracy and does not name timeout rates.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Code is public on jiho283/DialSim. No LICENSE file in the GitHub tree as of 2026-09-11. Dataset is a Google Drive zip. Many runs need OpenAI or Gemini keys.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Would prefer agents that keep a TV-show history under a wall-clock budget and abstain when the character could not know. That is hole 8 adjacent. It would not select a months-long companion store, identity drift after 50 sessions, poisoning, or two characters on one backend.

published_eval.name: DialSim / LongDialQA
published_eval.claimed_score: Paper v6. None of the agents scored above 60%. Table 3 Friends. Gemini 2.5 Flash Base LLM 53.94 (1.26). GPT-4o-mini BM25 Session Entire 52.11 (0.52). Fan-quiz 62.15% versus TKG 50.83% for Gemini 2.5 Flash. TKG two-hop 19.28%, oracle two-hop 51.74%. Name-swap drops BM25 Session Entire by 2.53 points on average (Table 4).
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Multiple-choice (or judged open-ended) accuracy of a TV-character agent on randomized questions during a long multi-party script, including unanswerable items. RAG versus long-context stuffing. Optional real-time timeout. Not companion identity, lore-as-lived, or poisoning.

open_unknowns: No LICENSE file in the GitHub listing. Dataset lives on Google Drive.
Paper v6 Table 3 does not report timeout fractions. Time budget is documented on dialsim.github.io and in simulator.py --sleep_time.
